questions.question: A frame of reference is made up of:
options: A stopwatch and a measuring tape
A reference point and a chosen positive direction
A starting speed and a finishing speed

questions.question: With the start as zero and north positive, the walker after 60 m north then 20 m south is at position:
A passenger on a moving bus is stationary relative to the seat and moving relative to the tar. This shows that:
options: Motion is described relative to a chosen frame of reference — both descriptions are correct
The road frame is the only true one
The seat's description is an illusion
The bus occupies two positions at once in one frame

questions.question: In a declared frame, the sign of a position tells you:
options: Whether the frame was chosen correctly
Which side of the reference point the object is on

questions.question: Distance and displacement are, respectively:
options: A scalar (path length) and a vector (change in position)

questions.question: For the 60 m north then 20 m south walk, the distance and displacement are:
One full lap of a 300 m track gives a displacement of:
options: Zero — the change in position is nothing

questions.question: Distance and the magnitude of displacement are equal only when:
options: The object ends where it began

questions.question: Average speed and average velocity are computed as:
options: Speed from displacement; velocity from distance
Speed from distance over time; velocity from displacement over time

questions.question: For the walk (80 m distance, 40 m north displacement, 80 s), the average speed is:
The average velocity for the same walk is:
A runner completes a 300 m lap in 75 s. Average speed and average velocity are:

subtopics.title: The Full Method, the Classic Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: Displacement is computed from:
options: The endpoints only — final position minus initial position
The sum of every path length
The longest leg of the trip

questions.question: A walker rests for 15 s during a journey. For average speed, the time used is:
options: The total time, rest included — the clock does not pause
The walking time minus the rest

questions.question: An answer of '0,5 m/s' to an average-velocity question is incomplete because:
options: Velocity is a vector, so the direction must be stated
The magnitude is too small to matter

questions.question: This vocabulary matters for later topics because:
options: Distance is the only quantity Grade 12 uses
Acceleration, the equations of motion and momentum are all built on velocity and displacement, the vectors

subtopics.title: Where Are You, Relative to What

questions.question: 'From the bus stop, three houses towards the river' illustrates that every position needs:
options: A reference point to measure from

questions.question: With the bus stop as zero and towards-the-river positive, the soccer field two houses the other way has position:
The minus sign in a position like −8 m means:
options: The object is on the negative-direction side of the reference point

questions.question: Physics settles the moving-bus riddle by:
options: Declaring the tar the true frame
Averaging the seat and road descriptions
Requiring you to declare a frame and stay loyal to it — both frames are legitimate

questions.question: In the two-instruments picture, the odometer and the pigeon measure, respectively:
options: Distance (every metre of the route) and displacement (straight line, start to finish)

questions.question: For the 60 m north, 20 m south walk, the odometer and pigeon readings are:
After a full lap of the track, the pigeon never leaves its perch because:
options: The runner was too fast to follow
Start and finish are the same point, so the displacement is zero

questions.question: The gap between the odometer's 80 m and the pigeon's 40 m was created by:
options: Turning back — the southward leg grew the distance while shrinking the net change of position

questions.question: The 'odometer over time' and 'pigeon over time' divisions give:
The walker's two averages, 1,0 m/s and 0,5 m/s north, differ by a factor of two because:
options: The clock ran differently for each
A quarter of the walking undid earlier walking, so the net progress was smaller than the path

questions.question: A delivery scooter weaves through town all afternoon and ends near its depot. Its averages will show:
options: A large speed and a tiny velocity
A small speed and a large velocity
